title: BLA Claims 13 Killed in Convoy Ambush, Bridge Blast Near Mastung's Khadkocha; Pakistan Confirms 2 Dead
detail: On the night of August 22, 2026, Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) militants detonated an IED that destroyed a Pakistani military armoured vehicle in the Khadkocha area of Mastung district, Balochistan, then ambushed a second armoured vehicle and its accompanying convoy. BLA spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said the group's 'Special Tactical Operations Squad' carried out the attack and claimed 13 security personnel killed and 10+ injured, with two armoured vehicles destroyed. Pakistani authorities did not match that toll: regional hospital sources said 2 bodies and 8 wounded personnel were brought to Nawab Ghaus Bakhsh Raisani Memorial Hospital in Mastung, with additional wounded airlifted to Combined Military Hospital (CMH) Quetta; a Dawn-network report described it as a single roadside IED in the nearby Goru area that killed 2 and injured 8, with no group claiming responsibility in that account. Separately the same night, unidentified attackers destroyed a culvert/bridge on the N-25 Quetta-Karachi highway near Injiri Cross-Khadkocha, disrupting traffic; no casualties were reported in that blast. The Balochistan Home Department imposed an indefinite curfew in Khadkocha and surrounding areas from 7:00 a.m. on August 23.

title: Suspected Drone Strike Kills 4 Laborers Near Mastung; Two More Bodies Found Shot
detail: Four laborers — Gul Khan Mugheri, Jehanzeb Abro, Ubaidullah Abro, and Imran Abro — were killed near the Anjiri area of Khadkocha, Mastung district, Balochistan, on the morning of August 22, 2026, in what survivors described as a drone or aerial projectile strike. Survivor Naseebullah Abro told reporters 'a projectile fell from the sky above us, and an explosion immediately occurred.' Police said the exact nature of the strike remained under investigation and did not confirm the drone attribution. Separately, two more bodies — unidentified at the time of reporting — were found shot dead in the nearby Garo area. The killings came the same week Pakistani security forces announced 37 Fitna al-Hindustan (Baloch separatist) militants killed in operations across Mastung, Mach, Khuzdar and Panjgur.
